A puzzle game with a distinctive style, [i] Alice’s Patchwork [/i] brought back memories of similar titles I used to play on web browsers and early mobile phones some 16 years ago. There’s a nostalgic charm to it. The game features six main chapters, each with 20 levels, for a total of 120 stages, with difficulty that gradually ramps up.

For casual players, it works perfectly as a relaxing experience—you can take your time solving puzzles while enjoying its soothing background music and unique art style. On the other hand, more hardcore players can approach it with a sense of urgency and challenge, since each level has three conditions for a “perfect” clear: complete the puzzle, make zero mistakes, and finish within a time limit.

As you progress, the difficulty increases significantly. Later puzzles can have over 60 pieces, yet the game only gives you six pieces at the start—the rest must be deduced through gameplay. If you’re aiming to perfect every level, it becomes a solid challenge. Many stages require repeated attempts; even if you memorize the final image, the pieces you’re given are randomized each time, demanding quick adaptation and strong dynamic memory.

That said, some levels feel excessively difficult—arguably to an unreasonable degree. Outside of brute-force repetition and memorization, it’s hard to rely purely on strategy for a first-time perfect clear, which somewhat undermines the spirit of a puzzle game. At this point, players can spend in-game currency to use hints or extend the timer by 30 seconds (costing 5000 coins each).

Still, these issues don’t overshadow what the game does best. As mentioned earlier, its standout strengths lie in its distinctive visual style and beautiful soundtrack. All 120 puzzles are based on classic, dreamlike scenes from [i] Alice in Wonderland [/i]. Simply restoring each image piece by piece while the music plays is already an enjoyable experience in itself—let alone the sense of surprise when the full picture finally comes together.

All in all, this is a very unique puzzle game, and I’d recommend it to anyone who enjoys the genre.

Es ist ein nettes Puzzlespiel. 
Ab und zu mal kann es frustrierend sein, weil man Teile "angereicht" bekommt, die an kein anderes angrenzen, wo man also einfach raten muss - in dem Fall habe ich immer die Hinweisfunktion benutzt oder erst versucht, andere zuzuordnen bis endlich der Bezug da war. Das geht schon und kommt auch nicht ständig vor. Die Zeit ist relativ knapp bemessen für jedes Level. Da ich trotzdem immer perfekt abschließen will (= keine Fehler und im Zeitlimit), habe ich meist erst zweimal durchgespielt, um mir alle Teile zu merken und dann erst auf die Zeit geachtet. Man kann sich auch mehr Zeit mit Spielpunkten erkaufen, die man für abgeschlossene Level bekommt. Ich komme damit gut hin. 

Blöd ist, dass es keine Speicherung in der Cloud gibt und ich mein Savefile einfach absolut nicht finden konnte: so musste ich nach einem PC Wechsel nochmal komplett von vorne anfangen, das hat ganz schön genervt und erklärt meine lange Spielzeit. (Ich bin noch nicht einmal ganz durch!) 

Die Hintergrundmusik ist ganz angenehm und die Grafik gefällt mir ebenfalls - alles ist so hergerichtet, dass es wie handgemacht aussieht, je nach Welt entweder aus Stoff, Papier, Holz, Stein... und auch der Soundeffekt beim Teilchen einfügen ist dem Material angepasst, das ist ein nettes Detail.

Es ist relativ umfangreich, vor allem wenn man es so perfektionistisch spielt wie ich, daher finde ich den Preis auch annähernd angemessen (als alter Geizkragen würde ich trotzdem auf ein Sonderangebot warten, ist ja auch kein "must-have").

🎮 《Alice's Patchwork》犀利点评：

《Alice's Patchwork》是一款由 Creobit 开发、8Floor 发行的拼图解谜游戏，于 2016 年 3 月 3 日发布，支持 Windows 平台。游戏以《爱丽丝梦游仙境》为背景，玩家将与爱丽丝和其他奇幻角色一起，在六个不同的场景中完成 120 个独特的拼图挑战。

🧩 核心玩法：拼图与探索的结合
游戏的主要玩法是将不同材质（如木头、布料、玻璃、纸张、宝石和金属）的拼图碎片组合成完整的图案。每个关卡提供五个可用的拼图碎片，玩家需要根据图案的形状和颜色，将其正确地放置在指定位置。游戏还设有计时模式和放松模式，满足不同玩家的需求。

✅ 优点：
丰富的内容：游戏包含 120 个独特的拼图关卡，提供超过 10 小时的游戏时间。

多样的材质：拼图碎片采用多种材质，增加了游戏的视觉多样性和挑战性。

放松的音乐：背景音乐舒缓，营造出轻松的游戏氛围。

适合所有年龄段：游戏操作简单，适合各个年龄段的玩家。

❌ 缺点：
界面设计一般：游戏的菜单和界面设计较为简洁，可能影响用户体验。

音乐变化较少：背景音乐种类有限，可能在长时间游玩后产生重复感。

成就系统存在问题：部分玩家反映游戏的成就系统存在无法完成的情况，可能影响成就收集者的体验。

🎯 总结：
《Alice's Patchwork》是一款结合了经典童话元素和拼图解谜的休闲游戏，适合喜欢拼图和放松游戏的玩家。尽管在界面设计和成就系统方面存在一些不足，但其丰富的内容和多样的材质仍值得一试。

⭐⭐⭐⭐（4/5）

В этом увлекательном приключении вы отправитесь в волшебный мир Страны чудес и Зазеркалья, где вам предстоит собрать мозаики в технике пэчворк, путешествуя с Алисой и знаменитыми героями из классических сказок.
В игре вам будет предложено собрать 120 мозаик, каждая из которых является частью большого приключения. Вы будете путешествовать по разным локациям, включая сады королевы Кровавой, леса Зазеркалья и даже подземелья Чеширского Кота. Каждая мозаика будет представлять собой головоломку, которую вам нужно будет решить, собирая кусочки в правильном порядке. Чем сложнее головоломка, тем больше очков вы получите за ее решение.

Графика в игре выполнена в ярких, насыщенных цветах, что создает атмосферу волшебства и чудес. Музыкальное сопровождение также соответствует теме игры, создавая ощущение приключения.

В целом это увлекательная и интересная игра, которая понравится как взрослым, так и детям. Она идеально подходит для тех, кто любит головоломки и приключения. Если вы готовы отправиться в волшебный мир Страны чудес и Зазеркалья, то эта игра для вас.

Alice's Patchwork is a mid quality jigsaw puzzle game that, unfortunately, falls short of its potential due to several frustrating design choices.

While the game could have been quite relaxing, it is marred by a global timer and other annoyances, such as an excessively high "price to pay"  achievements (like earning 1 million coins) and the challenges of obtaining 3 keys on many levels. The way the game distributes puzzle pieces makes it unnecessarily difficult, as they often don't match with anything already on the board, turning the hint button into a necessity rather than an option.
The game has a Relaxed mode without the timer, but that limits the maximum number of keys you can get/ world to 2, locking many achievements away from you.

The game's system is completely unbalanced, with incredibly low starting timers for each level, low earnings for each placed piece, and minimal rewards for saved seconds and other achievements. This imbalance makes the game stressful and time-consuming to complete.

Alice's Patchwork consists of 6 worlds with 20 puzzles each. The difficulty ramps up significantly after the first world, making them extremely challenging and often frustrating. Although the game starts peacefully with cliche pictures and easy levels, it quickly becomes overwhelming. 

The game struggles with its identity, oscillating between an easy-going vibe and an intense, almost punitive experience. Each level imposes a two to three-minute timer, and failing to complete the puzzle within this time results in a loud gunshot sound, adding unnecessary stress. You can't simply try placing pieces together to see if they fit; you must be absolutely certain before placing a piece, or you'll face the penalty.

Hints are available every 30 seconds and are essential to progress. Without using hints, completing the puzzles within the time limit is nearly impossible. Additionally, losing keys upon failure prevents progression, 

The developers expected players to replay levels, which might be acceptable in a game with replay value, but Alice's Patchwork lacks this aspect. Given the myriad of design flaws, it's hard to justify the $3 price tag, even for a game that could potentially offer 6-20 hours of gameplay.

In conclusion, Alice's Patchwork had the potential to be an enjoyable puzzle game but is ultimately bogged down by poor design choices and an unbalanced system. I would not recommend this game, as it is more likely to cause frustration than enjoyment. Save your time and money for a game that respects both.

This is my first time playing a mosaic/puzzle game, but even with my lack of knowledge on the genre, some really dumb things stand out about this game.

When I opened it up, It sounded very peaceful, and the pictures where pretty cliche, the first 3 or so levels where extremely easy. Then things got really stupid, really fast.

Its hard to tell if this game is trying to have a whole easy going vibe, or a really intense DOOM-like vibe. Because on each level your given a two to three minute timer, if you fail to do the puzzle in this time, you get shot. You literally get ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SHOT. S-H-O-T, like a gun, like you literally hear a loud shot go off. You may be thinking, welp why weren't you able to do any of the puzzles in 2-3 minutes. 

If so, good thought/question, if not, im going to answer it anyways. You can't just place pieces together to see if they line up. This means that you need to be absolutely. 100%, beyond positive, on your mothers grave, sure that the piece goes into that socket. If it doesn't, and feel free to says this with me, YOU GET ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SHOT. 

Instead of checking pieces that share similarities with one side of the board, you can use a hint every 30 or so seconds. You MUST use these hints. They are free, and allow you to speed run the puzzles, which again, you need to speed run or else you will get shot.

Every time I got shot I lost a key, and if I didn't have enough keys, I couldn't progress. Alternatively I needed 100,000 coins by the time I wanted to progress to World 4. I couldn't accomplish either. 

The developers expected me to replay this level, which in a game  with replay value, like Pizza Tower, which has a similar gimmick, would be fine. But this game has 0 replay value, and when you look at all these moronic mistakes by the developers its hard to justify the 3$, which isn't even that much for a 6-20 hours game, but is a hell of a lot for garbage like this.

I'm not one to smite down on a game in my reviews, but for this one, ill make an exception. Don't come within 5 miles of this trash, you will regret it.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

Alice's Patchwork is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs.  The game is a basic jigsaw/stained glass filling game, where you "colour" various 2D paintings (patchwork/tapestries apparently, it really doesn't matter) by tapping on the matching parts on your iPhone screen.  For some reason the developer decided to abuse Lewis Carrol's Alice in Wonderland, probably to help them scam PC gamers into buying mobile crap. 

From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.

There's no options to change the resolution for the mobile app or customise the graphics settings.  There's no way for gamers to ensure this mobile app is running at the native resolution of their displays... there's no guarantee this mobile app will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.  There's no way for gamers to try improve the low quality mobile phone graphics. 

The controls can't be customised because the game has such a dumbed down, simplified interface that it's just iPhone screen tapping stuff.  The fact that the interface is this dumbed down might be seen as a problem in itself, however... this is a fairly shallow experience if you're the kind of gamer that likes to play games with deep, rich control schemes and interaction.  You'll get none of that here.

Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the mobile app was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The mobile app is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.

These technical defects push this mobile app below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

You don't have to take my word about how bad the mobile app is, we can measure the interest in a game by how much people bothered to play it.  Alice's Patchwork has achievements, and they show us a very clear picture that the mobile app absolutely failed to capture any interest from gamers.  The most commonly and easily attained achievement is for completing the first tutorial set of games, but only around 6 percent of players bothered to get that far before uninstalling the mobile app.  That's a tiny, tiny proportion of gamers who even bothered with this.  Ouch.

Reviewing SteamDB to check how popular this mobile app was with players reveals a surprise... there's a very healthy spike in player counts for the mobile app.  But this isn't consistent with the achievement stats, that show only 6 percent of players bothered playing the mobile app for any reasonable amount of time.  How is it possible for this mobile app to have so many concurrent players who weren't even playing the mobile app?  Trading cards.  Players will use card idling software to collect the cards and sell them, but this won't trigger any achievements in-game.  That tells us people only really bought this mobile app for trading cards, and that's a damning indictment of the woeful quality.  A closer look at the numbers shows the mobile app just has a couple of players every week running up the mobile app and idling it for cards, then deleting it.  We must ask how it benefits gamers for there to be so many games like this, with no merit as a serious game, that only generate sales from people idling and selling the trading cards.

Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is $5 USD, on app stores, it's free. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a premium for a free mobile app just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  Because this can be played free elsewhere, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.  Who do they think we are?

I've nearly finished this one and my feelings on it are simple: if you want to play it for relaxation, it's an excellent puzzle game. If you lean more toward completionism and achievement hunting:

It comes with good achievements to get, but it's slow to get them. You will have to play most puzzles /at least/ twice - once to learn all the pieces and once more to meet the 0 mistake/time requirements. However, being quick enough means you are likely to slip up and place a piece slightly off at least once or twice when going for your 3-key score on each puzzle. If you do this, you have to start over to get your no-mistake key. 

Fortunately, hints are free and penalty free with a cooldown of about 15 seconds or something, so if you get a set of pieces where none are connected to the ones on the board, it will show you exactly where one of them goes. I feel like that's pretty generous.

All in all, I've had an okay time playing this. Probably the problem for me is that I sat down to binge the game and it's a better game for people who want to do a few puzzles a day for a long time. I just don't like this game enough to want to draw it out that long - hence the binging. If you want a slow paced puzzle game, this is perfect for you.

P.S. If you want to buy this because you love Alice in Wonderland, I warn you that only about 20% of the images are Alice in Wonderland related. The other ones are kind of naturey or fairytailesque, but not Alice.

Six worlds of beautiful mosaics with Alice and other famous characters of Wonderland and Looking-Glass Land. You have to assemble the uneven mosaic tiles to solve the puzzle. If you are able to solve the puzzle within a limited time and without any mistakes, you will get all three keys and some coins. Collect as many keys as you can to unlock a new world. 

If you have an excellent memory, you probably only have to play the level once or else you have to play multiple times to memorise the placement of the tiles so you can reduce spending coins to buy a hint. There is a free hint within a limited time, but if you wish to have more hints, either buy another one with the earned coins or wait for the next free hint after passing the limited time. 

If you want to enjoy the game in a more reasonable logic, you can tweak the settings on the configuration file (there is a guide available). The default setting is quite challenging to finish the puzzle within the given time without any mistakes. Overall, the game has beautiful graphic and good music although the default time seems slightly over than a reasonable challenge.

[h1]What this game is:[/h1] A themed puzzle game

[h1]How does it work?[/h1] There are 120 coloured puzzles to solve.  Each puzzle is made from an average of around 40 pieces.  You will get a handful of pre-set pieces on each board, and it is up to you to complete the rest. 

[h1]How does it perform?[/h1] Very easy to play. The game has two difficulty settings.  You have a competitive setting with a timer, and you have a relaxing setting with no timer, allowing you to to play at leisure without any stress.  You play mostly with your mouse.  One playthrough will get you between 16 to 20 hours of play.  

[h1]The good points:[/h1] Simple and inexpensive game.  The cutout of pieces in some puzzles is creative and confusing, increasing play difficulty.  Easy achievements to get, except the last two.  There are Steam trading cards.  Will run on a potato PC.  Takes only 320 MB of space on your HD.  

[h1]The bad points:[/h1] Playing movement is a bit fudgy which may become tiresome as it will put you out of position while placing a piece (creating a mistake, thus not allowing you an error free play). This also means placing pieces is a deliberate affair, so the game pacing is quite slow.  Last two achievements are grindy.  You will need to play the whole game almost twice in order to get to 1 million gold, which is not fun.  

[h1]My take on this:[/h1] If you like a cheap and relaxing game, this is it.  Buy this game when it is for sale, which happens from time to time.  I wouldn't buy it at full price, but can recommend it when at a serious discount.
